taxonomic_note: Current Kew POWO accepts Dermatophyllum secundiflorum. Sophora secundiflora, the name used in the B096 source row and in much Texas horticultural literature, is a synonym.
look_here_first: Evergreen limestone shrub or small tree with glossy pinnate leaves, dense hanging clusters of purple pea-flowers, and thick woody pods containing bright red seeds.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola natural-plants list records Sophora secundiflora as natural. Bexar — historical herbarium specimens from San Antonio/Bejar. Kendall — USDA GRIN wild accession from Tapatio Springs, Kendall County.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Historical synonym records are mapped to the accepted species; landscape plantings are not counted as native county evidence.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Fabaceae: alternate compound leaves, papilionoid pea-flowers, and legume pods.
best_field_traits: dense pendulous clusters of violet-purple papilionoid flowers
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with Lupinus texensis and Senna roemeriana, Texas mountain laurel is woody and evergreen. Its glossy pinnate leaves, hanging purple flower clusters, and woody seed pods make it unmistakable among local Fabaceae once mature.
